prompt: Make a separate scholarly Norse mythology illustration of Tanngrisnir, retaining the reference goat's natural shaggy grey-brown billy-goat anatomy, recurved horns and beard. Strengthen mythical identity through the explicit recorded episode, not invented animal anatomy: Tanngrisnir and the companion Tanngnjóstr pull the god Thor's chariot, attested in Poetic and Prose Edda (tanngrisnir-c01). Scene composition: Tanngrisnir is the foreground dominant goat in motion with all four coherent legs, one head, two horns and one tail; the second paler billy goat runs alongside at slightly greater distance. Both are visibly harnessed to a complete sturdy wooden two-wheeled chariot with Thor standing aboard, one hand holding the reins and the other carrying his short-handled hammer. Show a dramatic high mountain pass with towering cliffs and heavy storm clouds, mythical journey atmosphere but grounded natural materials. Full chariot and Thor must clearly be visible, not cropped to an empty wheel. Goat coats, Thor's reddish beard, plain wool cloak, carved wood and wrought fittings are editorial choices, not exact source iconography. No winged helmet, no goat wings/horns beyond normal horns, no generic neon, glowing eyes, aura, energy ribbons, smoke or invented elemental effects. Painterly naturalistic richly detailed mythic scene, square or portrait frame, no text, watermark, labels or gore.
